data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The expert will outperform the panel on the subset of verifiable tasks that require causal or mechanistic reasoning the checklist does not encode, because intuition can access latent task structure the checklist reduces to surface cues.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the task is fully captured by the checklist's explicit cues, the expert's latent access provides no marginal value.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's intuition is contaminated by bias (overconfidence, anchoring) that the checklist suppresses, the panel may dominate even on causal subsets.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the panel can learn to weight cues beyond rote compliance, it may approximate the expert's latent access.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist operationalizes explicit, verbalizable heuristics. But some verifiable tasks\u2014diagnosis, fault prediction, legal judgment\u2014require integrating tacit pattern-recognition over high-dimensional cues that the checklist either omits or compresses lossily. The expert's intuition, shaped by feedback over many cases, can weight these latent cues. The panel, constrained to the checklist, cannot. On the subset where latent cues dominate, the expert is systematically more reliable.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
